areas.areasCutEachNaming: areas cut from each naming style separately (packages and folders), split until no area holds most of the code
areas.areasCutNameSplit: areas cut by name, split until no area holds most of the code

importCoverageBar.importDataCoversCode: Import data covers {analysed} of {files} code files.
importCoverageBar.noneDependenciesCyclesRules: {phrase} {missingVerb} none: dependencies, cycles, rules and dead-code checks can miss them.

measures.afferentCouplingCountsImporting: Afferent coupling counts importing files; ranked by dependents (components) instead.
measures.efferentCouplingCountsImporting: Efferent coupling counts importing files; ranked by dependencies (components) instead.
measures.distinctShortestCyclesThrough: Distinct shortest cycles through it, each counted once.

recipes.howMuchCodeEach: How much code is in each language or file type?
recipes.extensionFileSuffixFiles: extension: the file suffix; files and lines per suffix.
recipes.howMuchProductionCode: How much is production code, tests, generated or third-party?
recipes.roleWhatFileScan: role: what a file is for, as the scan classified it.
recipes.whatTopLevelAreas: What are the top-level areas and how big is each?
recipes.areaFolderDepthFiles: area: the folder at that depth; files and lines under it.
recipes.whichBuildModulesPackages: Which build modules or packages does the project declare?
recipes.oneRowPerModule: One row per module a build file declares (pom.xml, package.json, go.mod…).
recipes.whichComponentsDoesNothing: Which components does nothing depend on (tops of the graph, entry points)?
recipes.nothingImportsTheseEither: Nothing imports these. Either entry points (apps, main, controllers) or unused code; dynamic loading is invisible to the scan.
recipes.whichPairsComponentsImport: Which pairs of components import each other?
recipes.eachPairTwoComponent: Each pair is a two-component cycle: the smallest tangle there is.
recipes.whichFilesMakeOne: Which files make one component import another?
recipes.filesReferenceHowMany: The files in `from` that reference `to`, with how many import references each (refs).
recipes.whichFilesHotspotsChanged: Which files are hotspots: changed often and complex?
recipes.hotspotChurnWeightedComplexity: hotspot: churn weighted by complexity. health: 10 is best.
recipes.whereEffortGoingUnhealthy: Where is effort going into unhealthy code?
recipes.healthBelowCountsUnhealthy: Health below this counts as unhealthy
recipes.filesBelowHealthLine: Files below the health line that still get commits: where debt costs time now.
recipes.whichProductionFilesHave: Which production files have not changed for a long time?
recipes.unchangedNotUnusedStable: Unchanged is not unused: stable code is often finished code.
recipes.whoMostActiveAuthors: Who are the most active authors?
recipes.commitCountsActivityNot: Commit counts are activity, not productivity.
recipes.author: author
recipes.howManyCommitsWere: How many commits were made per month?
recipes.distinctCommitsPerCalendar: Distinct commits per calendar month, newest first.
recipes.whichComponentsChangeTogether: Which components change together most often?
recipes.sharedCommitsCommitsTouching: shared_commits: commits touching both. pct: share of each side's own commits.
recipes.whichTypesClassesLargest: Which types or classes are the largest?
recipes.largestProductionFilesTypes: Largest production files; types = declared types in the file.
recipes.whatDoEngineS: What do the engine's rules report?
recipes.rulesEvaluatedScanTime: Rules evaluated at scan time, with the import that broke each.
recipes.whichComponentsHaveTests: Which components have tests and how much?
recipes.linesTestCodeFiled: Lines of test code filed under each component. Tests elsewhere (a separate test tree) count under their own component; this is not coverage.
recipes.howComponentsConnectedStatic: How are components connected: static imports, dynamic lookups, or type-only?
recipes.componentPairsHowOne: Component pairs by how one uses the other: a static import, only a runtime lookup by name, or only for types (erased at runtime).
recipes.whichImportsCouldScan: Which imports could the scan not resolve to code?
recipes.importsPointNothingScan: Imports that point at nothing the scan found: external packages, generated code, or blind spots. Many of these means the graph is missing edges.
recipes.whichOutsidePackagesLibraries: Which outside packages and libraries are imported most?
recipes.importedNamesNotComponents: Imported names that are not components of this snapshot, by how many files import them.
recipes.whichComponentsHaveNo: Which components have no tests in them or aimed at them?
recipes.whichTypesUsedMost: Which types are used from the most other folders?
recipes.typesReferencedOtherComponents: Types referenced from other components, by how many components and units use them.
recipes.whatChangedLast30: What changed in the last 30 days?
recipes.filesChanged30Days: Files changed in the 30 days before the scanned commit, most changed lines first.
recipes.whatPropagationCostHow: What is the propagation cost: how far does a change ripple on average?
recipes.shareComponentPairsWhere: The share of component pairs where one reaches the other through imports (itself included). Low single digits is loose; above 20–30% most changes can reach most code.
recipes.whatTypicalInstabilityDistance: What are the typical instability and distance from the main sequence?
recipes.mediansOverAllComponents: Medians over all components. Instability: 0 = everything depends on it, 1 = it depends on everything. Distance: 0 = balanced between abstract and stable.
recipes.whichCommitsTouchedMost: Which commits touched the most files?
recipes.commitsHowManyFiles: Commits by how many files they touched. Very large ones are usually renames, formatting or dependency bumps; the scan leaves the largest out of co-change.
recipes.whichClustersDoesDependency: Which clusters does the dependency graph fall into?
recipes.communitiesFoundEngineSets: Communities found by the engine: sets of components with more imports inside than out. A hint at modules, not a verdict; the lens builder weighs several readings.
recipes.whichBuildModulesDepend: Which build modules depend on which?
recipes.productionComponentsNoTest: Production components with no test file inside and no test file importing them. Tests reaching them indirectly are not counted.
recipes.buildModulesOtherModules: Build modules and the other modules of this repository each declares a dependency on.

revisions.rulesScopedEcosystemSo: Rules are scoped by ecosystem, so another language's rule no longer reads as kept.
revisions.vendoredGeneratedNonCode: Vendored, generated and non-code files are counted but no longer scored for health.
revisions.gitIdentitiesOnePerson: Git identities that are one person are merged by email.
revisions.phpKotlinDeclareUnits: PHP and Kotlin declare units; TypeScript workspace packages resolve to their source.
revisions.cycleCountsEachComponents: A cycle counts each of its components once; path lengths count hops.
revisions.gitHistoryFollowsRenames: Git history follows renames, so a moved file keeps its commits, age and authors.
revisions.timeWindowsCountBack: Time windows count back from the scanned commit, not from the day of the scan.
revisions.eachSnapshotRecordsCommit: Each snapshot records the commit, branch and uncommitted files it read.
revisions.coChangeNoLonger: Co-change no longer counts a component without commits as sharing all of its partner's.
revisions.filesCarryRoleProduction: Files carry a role (production, test, generated, third-party, non-code) and health scores keep their deductions.
revisions.snapshotsSayWhatWalker: Snapshots say what the walker left out, and how long each file has sat untouched.
revisions.snapshotsSmallerPairsFiles: Snapshots are smaller: pairs of files that never changed together are no longer stored, and Java class reachability is off.
revisions.workspaceSOwnIgnore: A workspace's own ignore patterns apply to its files and their history.
revisions.ambiguousRuntimeLookupResolves: An ambiguous runtime lookup resolves the same way on every scan.
revisions.indentationMeasuredWidthEach: Indentation is measured at the width each project uses (its Prettier config or .editorconfig, else the file's own), so two-space code is no longer read as half as deep.
revisions.swiftObjectiveCDart: Swift, Objective-C and Dart are read: iOS and Flutter code has components, edges and classes.
revisions.swiftPackagesXcodeTargets: Swift packages, Xcode targets and Dart packages are modules; Gradle modules are named by project path, and dependencies written as projects.x.y are read.
revisions.kotlinAnnotationsMarkDeclaration: Kotlin annotations mark the declaration they are written on, functions included, so composables are marked.
revisions.whatAppDeclaresPlatform: What an app declares to its platform (activities, permissions, URL schemes, entitlements) is recorded, and mobile apps are deployables with their stack.
revisions.analysisRevisionChangedHow: Analysis revision {r} changed how scans are read.
revisions.filePairsChangeTogether: File pairs that change together are recorded with how much of each side they cover.
